title: Maximum simulation time
overview: Provides the time threshold used by SimuIterState::Running when ctrl.iexitflag is nonzero. Ctrl::Init reads maxTime and initializes currTime to zero. In this branch, the outer loop stops when currTime reaches or exceeds maxTime; when iexitflag is zero, the stop condition instead uses maxSteps.
principle: maxTime is a simulation-time threshold, distinct from an iteration-count limit and from a residual-convergence criterion. Its unit and nondimensional scaling must be interpreted using the active case's time convention; the audited stop-condition code alone does not define those units.
architecture: Ctrl::Init loads maxTime into the shared solver control state and initializes currTime. SimuIterState::Running compares those values only in the nonzero iexitflag branch. This contract records the stop-condition wiring, not the full evolution law for currTime or every solver-specific time-step policy.

proves: Ctrl::Init reads maxTime as a Real value and initializes currTime to zero.
When ctrl.iexitflag is nonzero, SimuIterState::Running stops when ctrl.currTime is greater than or equal to ctrl.maxTime.
When ctrl.iexitflag is zero, SimuIterState::Running uses maxSteps instead of maxTime.
does_not_prove: The physical unit or nondimensional scale of maxTime for every solver and case.
The time-step selection or update law that advances currTime.
That maxTime is a residual-convergence criterion or guarantees a converged solution.
An admissible range or explicit positivity validation for maxTime.

verification.scope: Source-backed time-threshold loading and outer-loop stop-condition branch; no runtime test or physical-time interpretation is implied.

examples.title: Physical-time stop threshold example
examples.calculation: The active branch compares currTime >= maxTime. At 0.95 >= 1.0 the condition is false. If the physical-time update advances currTime to 1.0, the next running check becomes true.
examples.result: The configured outer-loop stop threshold is 1.0 in the active case time convention.
examples.limitations: The example does not specify the time unit or nondimensional scale, calculate the next time step, or prove that the final step is clipped exactly to maxTime.
